answer: Identity cost carry-forward: each new wallet inherits the unpaid dispute debts and penalty balance of every wallet that funded it, settled from its first earnings. An operator running many wallets thus pays each clone’s inherited liability before it can withdraw, making duplicate identities carry real timber from prior fraud. Enforcement reads funding and payout edges, so a vine of transfers cannot hide the chain. Every clone also forces the operator to reserve fresh capital against a growing atlas of tracked obligations.
